ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 19, 30, 289, 317 and 317-2; Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6570, as amended), Articles 2(8), 2(10), 5-3 and 9; Enforcement Decree of that Act; Prohibition of Financing for Offenses of Public Pressure Act (Act No. 7198, as amended); FATF Recommendations 24 and 25.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registration Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the company's registered place of business, Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize before a Korean notary public; then obtain an Apostille from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the destination state is party to the Hague Apostille Convention. For non-member destination states, do not apostille; obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by consular legalization at the destination state embassy or consulate in Korea. The two routes are parallel, mutually exclusive alternatives and are never applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Company Registration Extract and Active Status Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court Registration Office under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize before a Korean notary public; then obtain an Apostille from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention destination states. For non-Convention destination states, use Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by consular legalization at the destination state embassy or consulate in Korea. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive parallel routes and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chusik Hoesa Board of Directors, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute the board resolution and power of attorney, notarize it before a Korean notary public, and then either obtain a Hague Apostille from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs for member states or, for non-member states, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and subsequent consular legalization at the destination state embassy or consulate. Use only one route; never combine apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The Chusik Hoesa itself, with notarization by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the executed Articles of Association before a Korean notary public; then obtain an Apostille from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the receiving jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state. If the receiving jurisdiction is not a member state, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by consular legalization at the destination state embassy or consulate in Korea. The apostille route and consular route are alternative and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean licensed commercial bank maintaining the corporate account and seafarer payroll relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Have the issuing Korean bank branch notarize the officer's signature or execute a bank-issued authenticated letter; then obtain a Hague Apostille from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention destination states. For non-member destination states, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and consular legalization at the destination state embassy or consulate in Korea. Do not apply apostille and consular legalization in sequence; choose the route mandated by the destination state.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated List, Korea FIU watch-lists, and domestic sanctions and debarment registers must be completed before any UBO, director, signatory, crew principal, or counterparty is onboarded. PEPs and close associates require enhanced due diligence, documented source-of-wealth and source-of-funds analysis, senior management approval, ongoing transaction monitoring for high-risk maritime corridors, and immediate Suspicious Transaction Reports to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under Act No. 6570 as amended.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO) official company registry and automated corporate name search portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory trade name must be in Hangul, and the legal form suffix 'Chusik Hoesa' or, in English filings, 'Chusik Hoesa' or a statutorily recognized equivalent must be present at the end of the name. English transliteration follows the Revised Romanization of Korean. The four-tier naming convention generally comprises: (a) regional or brand indicator, (b) distinctive trade name, (c) business-object statement, and (d) legal form suffix. The name must not mislead as to business scope, nationality, or relationship with any state organ.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of receiving a written name rejection, the applicant may submit a written objection to the registry examination officer of the competent district court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act. The objection must set out the proposed name, statutory grounds for registrability, and a certified copy of the rejected application. If the registry officer affirms the rejection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the appellate court within two weeks. Retain all filing stamps and engage qualified Korean counsel; further judicial review is available only through extraordinary remedy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is effectively rejected for a maritime seafarer staffing and vessel crew management agency. The National Tax Service and Korean banks require actual management premises, visible signage, business records, seafarer dispatch files, payroll evidence, and a physical registered address under Commercial Act Article 30. A mailbox-only office will prevent corporate bank account opening, foreign currency wire processing, and issuance of the seafarer recruitment agency license under the Seafarers Act; Korean Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and National Tax Service inspectors treat a non-substantive registered office as a sham and may refuse or revoke the statutory license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: office lease in the company name, signage at the registered address, fixed business telephone and email, employment documentation for the representative director, seafarer dispatch agreements, crew employment records, payroll and social insurance filings, VAT invoices, vessel crew assignment logs, and the statutory crew recruitment agency license displayed on site. Quantified residual risk: 35% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months by the National Tax Service and/or the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries; risk rises materially if the registered office is a shared workspace or the company has no local operational staff.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, including Articles 289 (promotion and articles), 290 (statutory contents of articles), 291 (subscription inducement), 295 (registration of incorporation), 302 (incorporation meeting), and 317 (effect of incorporation registration), supplemented by the Commercial Registration Act and the Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act; the maritime staffing license is governed by the Seafarers Act, Chapter on Crew Recruitment and Supply Business (Articles 47 through 53), and for any incidental domestic non-seafarer placement services, the Employment Security Act Articles 18 through 21.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court or the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office in the Republic of Korea; subsequent tax registration is with the District Tax Office under the National Tax Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Chusik Hoesa) filed with the Commercial Registration Division under the Commercial Registration Act, accompanied by notarized Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act. A Chusik Hoesa may be incorporated with any issued capital amount stated in the Articles; there is no statutory minimum paid-in capital and no mandatory blocked escrow account for the registered capital. If capital is subscribed, the full value of issued shares must be paid into a bank account in the name of the company or promoter and evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit before filing. A separate financial guarantee may be imposed by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries for the seafarer recruitment and supply license; that guarantee is a licensing bond and is not a capital escrow.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: I, the secretary of the inaugural board meeting, hereby certify that the following resolutions were duly adopted by the Board of Directors of the corporation at a valid meeting held by unanimous written consent, with all directors present and voting in favor. RESOLVED, that the share capital subscription and allotment plan set out in the Articles of Incorporation be and hereby is ratified, confirmed and approved; that the directors are directed to verify that each subscription was made in writing, that the legally required subscription amount was paid to a bank account in favor of the company before registration, and that the bank certificate of deposit and the subscriber list are delivered to the representative director for filing with the court registration office. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is hereby established at the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation; that the representative director is authorized to execute any lease, license, or service agreement required for the registered office, to make all notices to registries, and to designate the registered office as the exclusive seat for all service of process, tax notifications, and regulatory summons. RESOLVED, that the banking authority of the company is hereby delegated to the representative director, with power to open, maintain, and change corporate settlement, payroll, foreign currency, and multi-currency crew payroll accounts; to execute signature cards and electronic banking mandates; to approve wire transfers and foreign exchange payments under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; and to engage a commercial bank in Korea for capital deposit and operational funds. RESOLVED, that the following initial statutory officers are appointed to hold office until the first annual general meeting and until their successors are elected: [Full Name], Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Full Name], Internal Director; [Full Name], Statutory Auditor; and [Full Name], Director. Each officer has delivered a written acceptance of appointment, and no officer is subject to any disqualification under the Commercial Act or the Seafarers Act. RESOLVED, that the officers be and hereby are directed to prepare and file the incorporation registration application with the competent District Court, obtain the business registration certificate, register the corporate seal with the relevant tax office, and apply for all maritime crew recruitment and supply business permits required by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, and to take any other corrective measure as may be necessary to secure full compliance with the corporate and employment regulations. I RESOLVED FURTHER, that this resolution may be executed in counterparts and may be attached to any contract, filing, or certificate as conclusive evidence of the officers' authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Review and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean corporate attorney and a Korean notary public; for foreign entity shareholders, the Apostille section of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Korean consulate or embassy in the shareholder's jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage Korean counsel to prepare the Articles of Incorporation (Chusik Hoesa) in conformity with the Commercial Act. The document must include all mandatory clauses: company exact name containing Chusik Hoesa in proper corporate form, purpose clause expressly covering maritime seafarer staffing, vessel crew management, crew recruitment agency services and related auxiliary services, the address of the registered office, total authorized shares, par value and series, initial issued capital, provisions on general meetings, board meetings, dividend rules, fiscal year, director and auditor limit, and methods of notice. Counsel and the promoters must verify whether any person or entity is disqualified to become a director or auditor. After shareholder sign-off, the Articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public; foreign shareholders should grant a power of attorney to a Korean agent and provide apostilled certification of existence and incumbency. Counsel should also prepare the promoter or subscriber vote form and the written consents appointing initial officers, to be signed simultaneously.
required_dossiers: Promoters or shareholders identification (passport or national ID copy)
Foreign entity certificate of existence and incumbency with apostille if applicable
Power of attorney to Korean counsel or notarized proxy
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean with official English translation
Subscribers list and share subscription forms
Written consents of initial directors and statutory auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary or counsel identifies a missing mandatory clause or an unlawful purpose clause, amend the Articles by addendum and resubmit for notarization before the incorporation meeting; if the defect is not curable by addendum, convene an extraordinary provisional meeting of promoters to adopt a corrective resolution and amend the Articles before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a Capital Contribution Bank Account and Payment of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A chartered commercial bank in the Republic of Korea (including Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori, Hana, or Industrial Bank of Korea) acting within the Financial Supervisory Service compliance framework.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a pre-registration account in the name of the promoters or the company-in-formation at the selected bank. Submit the notarized Articles of Incorporation, copies of the shareholders' identity documents, the subscription list, and proof of the registered office. The bank will perform customer due diligence and beneficial ownership verification. Each subscriber must remit the subscribed consideration in KRW or another freely convertible currency according to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The bank shall issue a certificate of deposit or account balance certificate in English if requested. Retain this certificate as conclusive proof of capital payment for the commercial registration and report the investment after registration if the shareholder is a foreign investor under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. No escrow lock-up is required by Korean corporate law, but the board must maintain this account as the company's registered capital contribution account until registration is complete.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate or personal identity documents and certificate of corporate authorization for subscribers
Subscription list and capital allocation schedule
Draft registered office lease
Beneficial ownership declaration and source of funds form
Certificate of foreign investment declaration if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's compliance department suspends opening due to insufficient beneficial ownership information, file an updated organizational chart, banking registry extract, or sworn declaration and resubmit; if the bank rejects the account, switch to another licensed bank and provide the same dossier to the compliance desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Statutory Incorporation Registration with the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court or the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; filing may be made electronically via the Commercial Registration Information System or at the court window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company with the court. The application must be signed by the representative director or Korean counsel with a power of attorney. Attach the full statutory dossier in chronological order: court application form, notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate or bank balance certificate, minutes of the promoters' meeting or incorporation meeting, appointment resolutions for directors and statutory auditor, written acceptance letters of each officer, identification copies, and proof of the registered office. The registrar examines whether the company name complies with the Commercial Act, whether the office is identified with an exact Korean address, whether the capital paid has been deposited, and whether each officer has legal capacity. If the application is in order, the registrar enters the company into the register and issues the certificate of registration, at which point the Chusik Hoesa acquires legal personality under Article 317 of the Commercial Act. This step should proceed no later than the day after the notarized Articles are available.
required_dossiers: Application for commercial registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of paid-in capital or bank balance certificate
Minutes of promoters' meeting or incorporators' meeting
Written acceptance of each director and auditor
Copy of registered office lease or ownership certificate
Power of attorney for legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a correction order, remedy the specific omission within the court's deadline, typically three to five business days, and resubmit the corrected or completed documents. If the registrar rejects the filing ex officio, file an immediate appeal against the registration official's decision with the District Court under the Commercial Registration Act; if the rejection arises from a non-waivable defect, withdraw the application and re-file with fully cured documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Corporate Seal Report, and Tax Posture Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent District Tax Office under the National Tax Service; local gu or county office for business place authorization; the Ministry of Employment and Labor for workplace registration if staff begin operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate business registration application to the District Tax Office through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal or in-person counter within the statutory period after incorporation. Include the certificate of incorporation registration, Articles of Incorporation, corporate officer identification, proof of office address, and the application for the business registration certificate. Report the corporate seal impression and retain the Korean and English versions of the business registration certificate, tax identification number, and VAT information. Register for electronic tax invoices, payroll income withholding, and social insurance (national pension, health insurance, employment insurance, industrial accident) with the respective authorities. Use the Korean Standard Industrial Classification code corresponding to maritime seafarer staffing and crew management, aligned with ISIC 5222, so that future licensing and tax reviews are consistent.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal impression card
Office lease agreement or occupancy certificate
Representative director identification and personal seal
Business registration application form prescribed by the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office flags a business classification mismatch, correct the KSIC code by filing a change application; if the corporate seal registration is rejected because of an invalid seal or address, obtain a registered seal stamp and re-file with the corrected lease agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Licensing of Seafarer Recruitment, Supply and Crew Management Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (Seafarer Policy Bureau) or the competent Regional Maritime Administration; the District Employment and Labor Office for any non-seafarer placement activity under the Employment Security Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After corporate formation, file the Seafarer Recruitment and Supply Business Permit application with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. The application must include a detailed business plan, evidence of financial ability or required security bond, the registered office lease and floor plan, the proposed seafarer labor contract forms, wage and repatriation terms, insurance cover including occupational accident and medical protection for seafarers, and appointment of a compliance officer who is qualified to meet maritime employment law requirements. The ministry may conduct a desk audit or inspect the office. The license decision is subject to a maximum statutory review period of 30 days. Once granted, the permit number must be quoted in contracts and advertisements. If the company also recruits domestic non-seafarer workers, obtain a paid employment placement business registration from the competent Employment and Labor Office. Maintain the corporate governance and licensing files in chronological order for annual compliance audits.
required_dossiers: Seafarer Recruitment and Supply Business Permit application
Certificate of incorporation registration and business registration certificate
Corporate register extract
Office lease, layout, and compliance staffing evidence
Financial security guarantee or bond certificate
Copy of the compliance officer's qualifications and appointment
Draft seafarer employment contracts and wage and repatriation standards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry requests supplemental documents, respond within the deadline; if the license is denied, obtain the written denial, correct the disqualification, replenish the guarantee, and re-file; if the denial is legally defective, appeal to the agency head and thereafter to the Administrative Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Seafarer Policy Bureau; for incidental employment placement, the Ministry of Employment and Labor; environmental permitting is not triggered for this service category.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Seafarer Recruitment and Supply Business Permit issued under the Seafarers Act; alternatively or additionally, a paid employment placement service registration under the Employment Security Act for non-seafarer placement activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Environmental Impact Assessment Support Division; local municipal environmental agencies
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. The licensed activity is maritime crew recruitment and vessel crew management, not physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing under ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx. No full environmental impact assessment report, preliminary environmental review, or environmental simple registration is triggered for a standard office facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable quantitative discharge limit exists for the ordinary office operations. The company must comply with the Waste Management Act by placing municipal solid waste and recyclables with licensed collectors; no industrial wastewater, volatile organic compounds, or hazardous waste streams are generated by the crewing function. If a vessel crew reception facility or seafarer accommodation is later operated, a separate environmental assessment and local building fire separation review will be required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable as a separate civil defense certificate for this office-based service, but the company must secure the building's fire evacuation and fire extinguisher readiness certificate from the building owner, comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act by appointing a safety and health manager for the office workforce, conducting an annual risk assessment,

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea, electronic portal via HomeTax System (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Chusik Hoesa in South Korea, the entity must first complete incorporation with the Commercial Registration Office. Subsequently, within 20 days of business commencement, the entity must apply for a Business Registration Number (BRN) at the local district tax office under the NTS. The application requires submission of the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, proof of foreign entity registration (e.g., certificate of good standing from home jurisdiction), and appointment of a domestic tax representative (if no permanent establishment). The BRN serves as both the Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the VAT registration number. The application can be filed online via HomeTax System or in person. Upon approval, the entity receives a BRN certificate, which must be used for all tax filings and invoicing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (South Korea does not offer check-the-box elections; however, a domestic group may elect consolidated corporate tax filing under the Corporate Tax Act, but this is not applicable to foreign entities. Hybrid mismatch rules under the OECD BEPS framework are implemented, but no elective mechanisms exist for foreign investors.)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 80 million annual turnover (approximately USD 60,000) for mandatory VAT registration; however, foreign entities providing services in Korea may be required to register regardless of threshold if they have a fixed place of business or are deemed to have a Korean establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (e-invoices) via HomeTax System for all B2B supplies. E-invoices must be issued within 5 days of the supply date. The system requires API integration for real-time validation and digital signature stamping to prevent fraud. There is no real-time fiscal clearance, but the NTS performs automated cross-checks of e-invoice data against VAT returns. Non-compliance with e-invoicing rules attracts penalties of up to 2% of the supply value.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to services supplied to non-residents for use outside South Korea, including maritime crew recruitment services for foreign vessels, provided the services are performed outside Korea or are directly related to export of goods. The service must be supplied to a foreign entity, payment must be received in foreign currency, and the service must not be consumed in Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Proof of Payment from Foreign Buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties for fraudulent or unverified export zero-rating claims include a penalty of 40% of the tax amount under the VAT Act, plus interest. Retrospective clawback of zero-rating benefits can be imposed for up to 5 years from the date of claim. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion may result in imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 100 million. The NTS conducts rigorous audits of export documentation, including cross-verification with customs and foreign exchange records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (The Central Bank of South Korea) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and designated foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a market-determined exchange-rate regime with full current-account convertibility and a regulated but progressively liberalized capital account. Residents and the Korean entity may make current-account payments if the payment is supported by genuine underlying invoices, contracts, or tax certificates, while capital-account transactions require filing, reporting, or approval through designated foreign exchange banks or the Bank of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Export proceeds are not confiscated or forcibly converted; a Korean export service company can retain foreign currency in domestic foreign-currency deposit accounts and use those funds for legitimate foreign-currency disbursements without surrender. Remittance of corporate profits and dividends is permitted after payment of Korean corporate income tax and withholding tax, provided the underlying foreign investment was duly reported and the bank receives the tax payment certificate, financial statements, and board-approved distribution resolution. For non-residents, the Korean won is not freely traded offshore for speculative purposes; onshore convertibility is supported by banking channels only. Capital inflows must carry a clear transaction purpose and investment declaration, and non-resident loans, derivatives, or direct investments may be subject to reporting thresholds. Overall, the regime balances open current-account flows with strict prudential surveillance on investment and FX hedging activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: General export receipts must be collected through a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank within 180 days from the date of export declaration unless an extension is granted under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the mandatory surrender ratio is 0%, allowing 100% of export proceeds to be retained in a foreign-currency deposit account or freely converted into Korean won at the prevailing market rate. For maritime crew recruitment and crew-management services, the corresponding service invoice and signed crewing contract must be presented so the bank can assign the correct foreign-exchange transaction purpose code when the receipt is settled.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Offshore digital EMI providers are not licensed banks or authorized foreign-exchange dealers under Korean law. The Korean entity cannot maintain a primary KRW operating account or capital verification account with an unlicensed EMI, nor can it execute statutory foreign-exchange reports through such a firm. The Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act restrict payment services to licensed domestic financial institutions. An offshore EMI may be used for low-value non-creditor bookkeeping convenience only in ancillary currency conversion or travel cards, but it can never act as the clearing intermediary for crew payroll, capital injection, or trade settlement. The legal route is a licensed tier-1 Korean bank account supported by the EMI as a secondary information channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed Korean stock corporation with non-resident or foreign statutory directors, physical in-branch appearance is generally mandatory, especially for capital escrow and cross-border foreign-exchange facilities. The statutory representative director should attend with the original passport, Alien Registration Card if resident in Korea, Korean corporate seal registration certificate, legalized/notarized Articles of Incorporation, shareholder register, and a valid foreign-investment report confirmation. Most tier-1 banks do not accept a remote consular proxy opening as the sole authentication; at most, a power of attorney can be accepted for a co-signatory, while the UBO or statutory director must still complete an initial on-site or documented video compliance interview with the bank's AML compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity in the Korean stock company, particularly where shares are held through foreign corporate managers, nominee shareholders, or a convoluted cross-border ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legalized Articles of Incorporation, current shareholder register and detailed ownership chart, Korean corporate registry certificate or equivalent foreign extract, notarized share-transfer records for all transfer events, government-issued passport/ID for every shareholder holding 10% or more, a certified UBO declaration using the standard FATF form, and a sworn source-of-wealth memorandum for the ultimate controlling party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Maritime sanctions exposure: crew nationality, vessel flag, charterparty owner, ship manager, port calls, or insurance arrangements involve a jurisdiction or entity subject to OFAC, EU, UN, or Korean government sanctions, including North Korea, Iran, Syria, Cuba, Crimea, or restricted cargo routes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete counterparty KYC pack for each shipowner, charterer, manning agent, and vessel: company registration certificates, director passports, vessel list with IMO numbers, flag-state maritime certificates, last 12 months of port-call logs, international ship registry extracts, a sanctions-screening report generated by a compliance screening engine at signing and each quarter, OFAC/EU/UN consolidated list match output, and a signed end-user declaration confirming no sanctioned individuals, entities, or cargo occupy the transaction chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of funds for the capital injection and initial working capital, especially when the remitting party is not the named foreign investor or when funds arrive from a third-party holding company with unrelated business purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of original bank statements from the instructing account, tax returns, audited financial statements or a certified public accountant's letter for the investor, notarized shareholder loan or gift documentation, an explanation of the investor's wealth accumulation and source of foreign currency, currency conversion or exchange records, and a Korean board resolution designating the exact purpose and amount of the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume or repetitive outbound cross-border payroll to many seafarer accounts in different jurisdictions without verifiable crewing employment, raising transaction-laundering and structuring concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid crew list, signed ILO Maritime Labour Convention 2006 seafarer employment agreements for every seafarer, sea service books and seafarer identity documents, valid STCW certificates, two-authorizer payroll instruction spreadsheets, the active ship-crew recruitment license issued by the Republic of Korea Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, bank transactional history for the prior 12 months, and a narrative explaining payroll seasonality, crew rotation, and any unusual variance in payment patterns.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor must first file the required foreign-investment report through a designated Korean foreign exchange bank or the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) before the capital wire is transmitted. Once reported, the investor sends a SWIFT MT103 from the original bank account to the Korean bank's capital escrow account, using SWIFT remittance fields to state the investor name, foreign investment declaration number, and foreign-exchange purpose code for direct investment capital. The receiving bank confirms the foreign currency inwards remittance, performs underlying documentation review and sanctions screening, and issues a foreign capital receipt certificate, which becomes the capital verification evidence for the Corporate Tax and FDI registration. A separate KRW current account can be funded by converting the foreign currency at the prevailing market exchange rate after the bank registers the conversion; the KRW conversion must be backed by the investment report and cannot be used for speculative offshore settlement or lending outside the declared business purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For seafarer payroll, the clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 per beneficiary or batched multi-currency payroll files through the Korean bank's treasury platform. For payments to non-resident shipowners or crewing principals, use SWIFT MT103, with MT202 cover for bank-to-bank reimbursements where required. Commercial letters of credit are appropriate where a charterparty or crewing service agreement contains payment guarantee conditions; the bank adjudicates the LC against presented shipping documents, crewing confirmation, invoice, and certificate of delivery of services. Documentary collections can be used for lower-value receivables, requiring the same set of original transport/crew-service documents. Each outbound transfer must be pre-screened for sanctions and assigned the statutory foreign-exchange payment purpose code; the bank retains the underlying contract, invoice, crew roster, and tax withholding confirmation to evidence the real business transaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore bank forward foreign-exchange contracts with a licensed domestic bank, covering up to 12 months of confirmed crewing receivables or payables, with the underlying invoice/contract submitted and no speculative position allowed.

Plain-vanilla foreign exchange option contracts in KRW/USD, KRW/EUR, or KRW/JPY purchased or sold to hedge actual commercial exposures, where the premium is paid from the KRW operating account and the net option position does not exceed the underlying trade cash flow.

Cross-currency swaps for protection against long-term mismatches between foreign-currency capital or debt obligations and KRW operating income, subject to external debt reporting thresholds and Bank of Korea approval where the notional exceeds the filing limit.

Offshore non-deliverable KRW forward (NDF) transactions are restricted for speculative non-resident accounts; a resident Korean corporation may transact an NDF only where a domestic licensed bank confirms a real trade or investment exposure, documents the underlying transaction, and signs the NDF through the onshore branch as a covered hedge.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with balance sheet, income statement, corporate tax computation schedules, and statutory financial statement attachments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea (NTS) via Hometax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year close, no later than March 31 of the immediately following year; for non-calendar fiscal years, the filing deadline is the last day of the third month following the fiscal year close, with an approved extension of up to one month if applied before the original due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of the assessed corporate income tax; under-reporting triggers an additional tax of 10%, with 40% for intentional or grossly negligent misstatement; unpaid corporate income tax accrues daily late-payment interest at 0.022% per day, and continued delinquency after formal demand and asset seizure can lead to compulsory dissolution and administrative strike-off of the Chusik Hoesa from the Korean commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surcharge return and payment corresponding to the 10% local tax surcharge on central corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Si-Gun-Gu local government office via WeTax local tax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory due date as the central corporate income tax return, being March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year, with the same approved extension period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or pay the local surcharge attracts a non-filing additional tax of 20% of the unpaid local tax, under-reporting penalties of 10%, and daily late-payment additional charges; persistent delinquency can result in forced collection against corporate bank accounts, registration liens, and eventual dissolution proceedings against the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minutes of the annual ordinary general shareholders' meeting, board resolution on the annual financial statements, approval of the statutory auditor, and registration of any director or representative director changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Commercial Registry of the district court under the Supreme Court of Korea for registrable changes; minutes and resolutions remain at the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ordinary general shareholders' meeting must be convened within three months after the close of the fiscal year, which is March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year; any change in directors, representative directors, or registered corporate facts must be filed with the commercial registry within two weeks from the date of the change or resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the ordinary general meeting enables a shareholder to petition the court for permission to convene the meeting; failure to register director changes means the unregistered representative cannot oppose bona fide third-party claims, and each director who fails to discharge governance duties may be liable to the company and shareholders for resulting damages; persistent noncompliance can trigger court-supervised involuntary closure and registration cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified CPA audit report on annual financial statements and, if subject to the external audit regime, filing of the audited financial statements on the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service via DART and the Securities and Futures Commission for audit oversight
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The statutory audit must be completed within four months after the fiscal year close, which is April 30 for a December 31 fiscal year, and the audited financial statements must be submitted to the ordinary shareholders' meeting; DART filing is required within fifteen days after approval at the shareholders' meeting when the company is subject to external audit reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company subject to external audit that fails to appoint a certified auditor or fails to file audited statements is exposed to administrative fines up to KRW 30 million, corrective directives from the Financial Supervisory Service, and potential disqualification of the ship-crewing agency from maritime industry licensing renewal and foreign-flag principal contracts; deliberately false audit reporting carries criminal penalties under the Act on External Audit of Joint-Stock Corporations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual value-added tax returns for the crew recruitment agency's taxable and zero-rated maritime services, including electronic tax invoice totals and related VAT schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea (NTS) via Hometax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the first calendar tax period, final VAT return by July 25 and preliminary return for January through March by April 25; for the second calendar tax period, final VAT return by January 25 of the following year and preliminary return for July through September by October 25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or under-declaration in the VAT return triggers an additional tax equal to 10% of the unpaid or unreported VAT; overdue VAT accrues daily late-payment additional charges at 0.022% per day; enforced collection measures including garnishment of receivables from foreign shipping principals and seizure of corporate assets may ultimately lead to the involuntary dissolution of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership annual confirmation and bank counterparty AML due diligence declaration, together with updated entry in the shareholder register for any share transfer during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit, financial institutions, and banks currently maintaining the corporation's multi-currency payroll and Swift wire accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial bank customer due diligence confirmation must occur within 30 days of account opening, and any subsequent change in beneficial ownership or control structure must be reported to the relevant bank within 30 days; a consolidated annual UBO declaration is required as part of the bank's ongoing customer due diligence at least once every calendar year, typically before December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to identify or disclose a beneficial owner under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and AML/CFT reporting rules can result in administrative fines of up to KRW 30 million, suspension or closure of the company's payroll and swift payment accounts, and criminal liability for officers who knowingly conceal the controlling person in financial transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual operating and business performance report for the maritime seafarer staffing and crew recruitment license, including placement statistics, seafarer employment register updates, and proof of maintained crew recruitment bond or insurance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries through the relevant Regional Office of Oceans and Fisheries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 45 days after the end of the calendar year, meaning no later than February 14 for a December 31 year-end, unless the licensing authority specifies an alternate annual report date in the seafarer recruitment business registration certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual business performance report may trigger administrative suspension of the crew recruitment license for up to six months, cancellation of the seafarer staffing registration, and forfeiture of the right to recruit seafarers; operating without or after revocation of the required license is a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment of up to two years or a criminal fine of up to KRW 50 million.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Joint-Stock Corporations, an independent certified CPA audit is legally mandatory when the Chusik Hoesa has total assets of at least KRW 12 billion approximately USD 9.2 million at the end of the fiscal year; when the corporation is listed on KOSPI, KOSDAQ, or KONEX; when it is a bank, financial holding company, insurer, securities firm, or another statutory public-interest entity; or when the Securities and Futures Commission orders appointment of an external auditor. The Korean external audit law does not create a standalone turnover-only or headcount-only trigger for unlisted companies, but turnover and employment headcount data are used in the audit-exemption classification for small and medium-sized corporations; the core quantitative balance-sheet threshold remains total assets of at least KRW 12 billion, and the audit duty also extends to a controlling corporation whose consolidated total assets satisfy the same KRW 12 billion threshold. Shareholders holding not less than 3% of issued shares can also demand an external audit report, and foreign maritime principals entering multi-currency payroll arrangements may require an audit certificate even when the statutory threshold is not reached.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS for public-interest entities and listed stock corporations, and K-GAAP or the Korean Accounting Standards for Small and Medium-Sized Companies for non-listed private Chusik Hoesa companies; financial statements must be prepared on an accrual basis under Korean commercial and tax accounting principles and audited in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not maintain a public standalone UBO filing for a non-listed Chusik Hoesa; annual beneficial ownership confirmation is achieved through the board's certification of the shareholder register at the ordinary general shareholders' meeting and through the company's obligation to respond to bank and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit customer due diligence requests. Any transfer of shares or change of controlling beneficial ownership must be entered in the shareholder register at the company without delay and must be communicated to the company's banking counterparties within 30 days; a consolidated annual beneficial ownership declaration is required by each bank maintaining the Swift wire and multi-currency payroll accounts at least annually and no later than December 31 of each calendar year. The company must maintain at its registered office the current shareholder ledger, the transfer book, and supporting instruments of transfer for each registered share movement.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 to USD 1,800 per year for a commercial registered-office address and local corporate management agent, depending on district, service scope, and mail handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 to USD 35,000 per year for a full certified audit under K-IFRS or K-GAAP by a national or Big4 audit firm; USD 4,000 to USD 8,000 per year for an agreed-upon procedures or reviewed compiled financial statement package for a non-listed Chusik Hoesa below the statutory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Top combined statutory effective rate 27.5% (25% national Corporate Income Tax plus 10% Local Income Tax surtax levied on the national CIT amount); national CIT bracketed rates are 10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 20% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 22% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 25% on the excess over KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea offers preferential tax regimes under the Special Tax Treatment Control Law and related free-zone statutes. Eligible Foreign Investment Zones and Free Economic Zones foreign-invested enterprises may obtain 100% exemption of corporate income tax for the first five years and a 50% exemption for the following two years for qualified foreign investment. R&D tax credits are available for qualifying R&D costs, including enhanced SME credits; fiscal incentives also exist for job creation, facility investment, and technology income. No patent box regime exists, but technology-transfer income may be separately exempted or reduced under STTCL. Pure maritime crew recruitment agencies do not qualify for tonnage tax unless they own or operate the relevant ships.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Return, prescribed by the National Tax Service and filed through the HomeTax electronic filing portal (homtax.go.kr). The return is accompanied by local income tax return schedules and, for non-resident payments, withholding tax schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing; quarterly interim prepayments are required where the prior-year corporate tax liability exceeds KRW 5 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed and the tax paid by the last day of the third month following the fiscal-year-end. For a calendar-year corporation the statutory deadline is March 31. A one-month extension may be granted upon timely application to the NTS, moving the filing due date to April 30 for calendar-year filers; interest continues to accrue on unpaid tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identification and Fiscal Year Header
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Chusik Hoesa, business registration number, representative director, corporate registered address, fiscal year start and end, and government industrial classification code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the ultimate non-resident shareholder and any foreign parent; file under the exact Korean legal entity registered with the Korean court. Use a classification code that aligns with ISIC 5222 and the statutory ship crew recruitment license. Inconsistency between the NTS registration, the maritime labor authority license, and the printed corporate name triggers examinations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax accounting begins with net income per the Korean GAAP or K-IFRS financial statements reported for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize crew recruitment, payroll facilitation, and vessel management fees as service revenue when earned and collected, not on a cash basis. Do not net out wages paid to seafarers as mere collections unless the Korean entity has clear payroll agency authority. Cross-border payment flows received through offshore accounts must be fully included; Korea taxes worldwide income of a domestic corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Taxable Income Reconciliation and Add-Back Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of financial net income to taxable income: add-back non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation adjustments, donations exceeding limits, entertainment expenses, and tax-exempt income exclusions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back related-party management fees, royalties, interest, or captive insurance charges paid to non-resident affiliates unless the Korean taxpayer can substantiate commercial purpose, actual receipt of service, arm's-length pricing, and withholding compliance. Fees lacking substance or paid to zero/low-tax jurisdictions are recharacterized by the NTS as dividends or non-deductible profit distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Loss Carryforward and Tax Base Determination
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory tax base equals reconciled taxable income less allowable carried-forward tax losses from prior years and any permitted special reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only losses carried forward within the statutory 10-year period and respect the annual cap applicable to non-SME corporations. If the company participated in a merger or acquisition, ensure the continuity-of-business conditions in the Corporate Tax Act are met; otherwise the NTS will deny the deduction. A foreign-parent restructuring that changes the ultimate beneficiary may be treated as a deemed disposal termination of loss carryforwards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Progressive Corporate Tax and Local Income Tax Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive CIT brackets to the taxable income; compute national CIT due and the 10% Local Income Tax surtax; subtract prepayments to determine final balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the tax using the statutory national rates and add the local surtax. For a Korean subsidiary owned by non-residents, dividends received from other domestic corporations may be subject to no significant tax exclusion; review the special affiliated-company dividend exclusion rules carefully. A Foreign Tax Credit must be claimed through this box for withholding taxes withheld by other jurisdictions on foreign-source crew fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Credits and Statutory Incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detail of R&D tax credits, job creation credits, employment subsidies, foreign tax credits, and other permitted credits reducing the computed tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The crew agency can claim R&D credits only for genuinely technical projects conducted in Korea by Korean employees; expense labels on seafarer training do not qualify. FEZ foreign-investment exemptions require an approved foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Any credit dependent on foreign ownership percentage must match the registered non-resident ownership certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Outbound Payments to Non-Residents and Withholding Certification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separate schedule of dividend distributions, interest payments, royalty payments, and other outbound payments to non-resident related entities and beneficial owners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report every remittance to a non-resident shareholder, lender, or licensor in the NTS foreign-payment system. If treaty relief is claimed, attach the foreign Tax Residency Certificate and a beneficial ownership declaration; otherwise withhold the statutory 22% combined rate. A failure to attach treaty forms is treated by the NTS as an unjustified tax benefit with penalties and interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Attachments, Transfer Pricing Disclosures, and Director Certification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statements, audit report if statutory, income reconciliation schedule, transfer pricing documentation, CFC disclosures, and director declaration of accuracy.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Local File and Master File when the thresholds are met, accompanied by a comparability analysis for all cross-border crew-management transactions. Foreign-controlled Korean companies should attach an economic-substance narrative describing local recruitment offices, licensed brokers, and Core Income-Generating Activities. The representative director must sign under civil and criminal penalties for false tax filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or under-reporting triggers negligence additional tax under the Corporate Tax Act of 20% of the under-reported tax in ordinary cases and 40% in cases of deliberate concealment or gross negligence. Unpaid corporate tax bears statutory overdue interest currently calculated at a daily rate of approximately 0.022% (annualized as specified by NTS for the relevant period) until payment. Fraudulent filing or preparing false tax returns violates the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and is punishable by imprisonment for up to five years and/or a fine up to five times the amount of tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% combined rate on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% Local Income Tax surtax (10% of the 20% national withholding). An applicable bilateral income tax treaty may reduce the rate to between 5% and 15%, generally requiring a 10% or higher shareholding for the lower treaty rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: DTA relief is not automatic. The non-resident beneficial owner must (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction, (2) execute a beneficial ownership declaration confirming that it is not a conduit and has economic capacity and real ownership of the income, (3) submit the original or certified copies to the Korean payor before payment, and (4) have the Korean payor attach the completed NTS treaty-relief application to the withholding return filed through HomeTax. If the relief is not established before the withholding return, the Korean withholding agent must withhold the full 22% statutory rate; the non-resident may then file a domestic refund claim with the district tax office within three years from the statutory return due date or invoke the competent authority mutual agreement procedure under the treaty. The NTS will deny treaty relief where the recipient lacks substance or where the dividend, interest, or royalty is attributable to a Korean permanent establishment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on cross-border interest and royalties is 20% national withholding tax plus 2% Local Income Tax surtax, giving a 22% combined gross-basis rate. Treaty rates vary: interest is commonly reduced to 10% or 15%, and royalties are commonly reduced to 10%, provided the non-resident is the beneficial owner and the income is not effectively connected with a Korean permanent establishment. For a crew recruitment company, payments characterized as technology royalties for crewing software, crew-database access, or vessel-management systems will be heavily scrutinized for actual intangible ownership, transfer-pricing benchmarks, and substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Korean taxpayer included in an MNE group with consolidated group revenue of KRW 100 billion or more is generally required to prepare a Master File. A Local File becomes mandatory when cross-border intercompany transactions in goods reach KRW 50 billion, when related-party services or loans reach KRW 10 billion, and when intangible-related transactions reach KRW 5 billion in a fiscal year. Country-by-Country reporting applies when the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 1 trillion. Below these thresholds, contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation is still recommended for maritime crew-management fee arrangements with overseas shipowners or foreign affiliates.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 14 and the Corporate Tax Act Article 4 establish a substance-over-form doctrine and a general anti-abuse rule. The NTS and the courts disregard transactions whose only purpose is tax avoidance. For a ship crew recruitment agency, Core Income-Generating Activities include identifying qualified seafarers, interviewing and vetting crew, negotiating employment conditions, managing payroll, coordinating visas and certificates, supervising vessel deployment, and maintaining contracts with shipowners. These functions must be carried out in Korea by local employees through a staffed office; a Korean entity that merely invoices while all CIGA is performed by a foreign affiliate in a tax haven will be
